message.content:
The TLS search function is in the TCP payload callback buffer. Since our packet has payload, it will be called. Good.

Now, there's the concern about the "giveup" check at the end of `ndpi_detection_process_packet`:
```c
if((flow->num_processed_pkts == 1) && (ret.master_protocol == NDPI_PROTOCOL_UNKNOWN) &&
   (ret.app_protocol == NDPI_PROTOCOL_UNKNOWN) && packet->tcp && (packet->tcp->syn == 0) &&
   (flow->guessed_protocol_id == 0)) {
  ret = ndpi_detection_giveup(ndpi_str, flow, 0, &protocol_was_guessed);
}
```

For this to not give up, either `ret.app_protocol != NDPI_PROTOCOL_UNKNOWN` (TLS detected) or `packet->tcp->syn != 0` or `flow->guessed_protocol_id != 0`.

Since our packet is not a SYN, and if TLS is detected during `ndpi_check_flow_func`, then `ret.app_protocol` will be set to TLS. Let me verify that `ndpi_search_tls_tcp` sets the detected protocol.

Actually, `ndpi_int_tls_add_connection` is called in `processTLSBlock` for the Server Hello. This sets `flow->detected_protocol_stack[0] = NDPI_PROTOCOL_TLS`. So after processing, `ret.app_protocol` will be TLS. Good.
